title: Codesign for Broadcast Addressing Biochip Towards Tamper-Resistance and Enhanced Reliability
problem: Digital Microfluidic Biochips (DMFB) using broadcast addressing are vulnerable to actuation sequence tampering attacks that manipulate assay results. Existing tamper-resistance solutions lack feasible wire-routing implementations. Higher electrode switching activity degrades reliability.
motivation: DMFB devices are critical for biomedical and clinical applications requiring both security and reliability. Attackers can stealthily tamper with actuation sequences to corrupt results. A codesign approach addressing design, security, and reliability simultaneously is needed.
method: Novel pin-mapping method for broadcast addressing biochips that jointly optimizes: (1) tamper-resistance via stealthy attack detection, (2) feasible wire-routing solutions, (3) reduced switching toggles for enhanced reliability.
key_novelty: First pin-mapping method combining tamper-resistance, wire-routing feasibility, and reliability optimization for broadcast addressing DMFBs.
contributions: Introduced first pin-mapping method for broadcast addressing addressing combined design-security-reliability challenges
Improved tamper-resistance metrics compared to state-of-the-art
Provided feasible wire-routing solution previously lacking in literature
Reduced electrode switching toggles to enhance chip reliability
baselines: State-of-the-art tamper-resistant designs without routing feasibility
limitations: Specific quantitative improvements not provided in abstract
Limited to broadcast addressing scheme; applicability to other addressing schemes unclear
No experimental validation on fabricated biochips
Does not address other attack vectors (e.g., timing side-channels, power analysis)
